_comment: Example Project Diana configuration.
This file is optional -- every setting below already has a working default
in diana/config.py. Copy it to config.json and edit only what you need:
cp config.example.json config.json
Then run with:  python -m diana.main --config config.json
Anything you leave out falls back to the default. Setting a key here that
does not exist in Config is a hard error on purpose, so a typo is loud
rather than silently ignored.

audio._comment: Must match the model's native rate. Vosk small en-us is 16000.

wake._comment: Keep this short. Every extra phrase enlarges the search space.

_comment: post_wake_discard_ms: audio thrown away right after the wake word, so
your first syllable does not get mistaken for part of the command.
show_partials: print the in-progress transcript while you speak.
wake_response: what she says when she hears her name.
command_handler: 'intents' (default) runs the rule grammar, so a
command produces an EVENT code and she says what happened.
'print' is the original V0 handler, which only repeats what it heard.
command_reply: 'intent' (default) says what happened -- 'lights are now
on.' 'echo' repeats the command verbatim, which is the best way to
spot a mishearing, so keep it available. 'ack' says a short varied
'Okay.' and 'none' stays silent.
command_show_events: print the 'EVENT: LIGHTS_ON' line. This is the
machine-readable half of the output and the one place a decision is
unambiguous, so leave it on.
command_known is the set of commands Diana claims to support. null
(the default) means everything is, which is the honest setting -- the
grammar already declines anything it cannot do. Set it to a list and
anything outside it gets command_unsupported_response instead.
command_placeholder_response is said for things that are understood but
have no real source behind them yet, like weather.
command.command_unsupported_response: I don't know how to do that yet.
command.command_placeholder_response: I don't have a real source for that yet.

_comment: Fallback conversation. When the grammar matches nothing, the utterance
was probably not a command, so it goes to a small local model
instead of getting 'I don't know how to do that yet.'
The model only ever answers. It has no access to the device registry,
cannot emit an event code and cannot act on the house -- a command is
handled by the grammar or not at all.
Requires Ollama running locally, with the model already pulled:
ollama serve
ollama pull qwen2.5:0.5b
Check it with:  make chat-test
Set chat_enabled to false and everything else still works, with no
network and no server of any kind.
chat_timeout_s is deliberately short. A voice assistant that waits
thirty seconds for a reply has failed more completely than one that
admits it did not get one.
chat_host must stay on localhost. Pointing it anywhere else sends what
you say to your microphone to a third party.
chat.chat_unavailable_response: I didn't catch an answer to that.

_comment: Text-to-speech. 'auto' speaks if a voice is installed and prints
otherwise, so this section can be left alone entirely.
Fetch a voice with:  python download_models.py --voices
